mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound from -28.4 at t-1w to -5.9 at t-0w signals reduced fear of outdoor exposure and normalization of local movement; this spillover lifts discretionary retail and recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
regime_hint: early reopening and spring outdoor normalization
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by more than 20 points in one week but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing above zero at t-0w (+0.4 after -5.6 at t-1w) indicates essential-trip demand has stabilized and panic stockpiling is waning; with essential logistics restored, consumers re-enter non-essential retail, so RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive (t-0w = +0.4 after t-1w = -5.6)
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is flat or lower than its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Steepening WORKPLACES decline (-25.1 to -32.7) combined with rising RESIDENTIAL (17.0 to 18.1) indicates intensified stay-at-home enforcement; because workers remain home, weekday retail and recreation trips are suppressed, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks relative to the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES t-1w to t-0w = -7.6 and RESIDENTIAL t-1w to t-0w = +1.1
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains near its trough at -36.0 and is nearly flat versus t-1w (-37.3), indicating no restoration of broad mobility access; because discretionary retail and recreation trips often depend on transit, RETAIL_REC remains below its last four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -30 for four weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has crossed above the last four-week mean (-28.0), reaching -26.4 at t-0w after -30.4 at t-1w; this upward momentum indicates behavioral adaptation to restrictions, and the improvement continues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC t-0w > -28.0 (the last 28-day mean) by at least 1 point
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC is at least 1 point above its last 28-day mean but the next 14-day mean is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility turning strongly upward relative to winter baseline (-5.9 at t-0w) reflects seasonal spring weather and longer daylight; outdoor activity increases general retail traffic even while indoor malls remain constrained, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS exceeds -10 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Under stringent stay-at-home orders, RESIDENTIAL above +15 and WORKPLACES below -25 jointly indicate that remote work and home confinement dominate; this regime keeps RETAIL_REC depressed for four weeks regardless of small PARKS gains.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL > 15 and WORKPLACES < -25, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Divergence between PARKS recovery (-5.9) and TRANSIT depression (-36.0) indicates that outdoor recreation has resumed locally while broader travel remains suppressed; without transit recovery, retail-and-recreation catch-up is limited, so RETAIL_REC stays below its last four-week mean over the next one week.
failure_condition: If PARKS > -10 and TRANSIT < -30, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its last 28-day mean.
